candidates.tagline: Fashion giant ditched its photo team for AI — AI embedded the pants in the shoes
candidates.story: In 2026, luxury fashion e-commerce SSENSE replaced its entire photo and makeup team with AI during court-supervised restructuring; the AI published product images where designer Gerrit Jacob leather pants appeared with their graphic print smeared, random hallucinated seams, and the trousers seemingly tucked impossibly into the soles of the model's shoes — designers publicly called them out on Instagram, and SSENSE pulled the photos.
candidates.why_funny: SSENSE built its reputation on elevated, impeccable fashion photography — the AI they replaced the entire team with made the clothes look physically impossible to put on a human body.
candidates.alt: Screenshot of SSENSE product page showing AI-generated Gerrit Jacob leather pants with graphic print smeared and the trousers apparently tucked into the soles of the model's shoes — an AI hallucination from the retailer's replacement photo system

candidates.tagline: Amazon made Kindle's back panel easy to swap — now it falls off in the case
candidates.story: Amazon's 2026 Kindle redesign added a removable back panel to comply with EU right-to-repair battery-replacement rules; Mashable testing found the panel pops off when the device is pulled from a tight case — Amazon's official response: 'If the back panel accidentally comes off, it does not mean the device is broken; just press it firmly back into place at all four corners.'
candidates.why_funny: Amazon made the Kindle 'repair-friendly' by designing a back that detaches for battery swaps — but it also detaches when you take it out of a case, so the fix for the EU repair mandate is now its own repair problem.
candidates.alt: Amazon Kindle 2026 e-reader showing its redesigned flush-glass front and the new removable back panel added for EU right-to-repair battery-replacement compliance — the same panel that testers found pops off accidentally when the device is removed from a tight case
